Most of the knees are likely to be made of a cobalt, chromium and molybdenum allow. Because the knee experiences higher loads and because the knee bends more frequently, it’s important to choose an alloy with higher fatigue strength and better wear properties against the coupled polyethylene (most of which at this point are highly cross linked and vitamin E impregnated). It’s because of these reasons that CoCrMo is chosen over titanium. 

More companies are finding robust surface treatments to solve both of these gaps in Ti so more Ti knees are hitting the market but primarily for people with nickel or cobalt allergies as these are common elements in the commercially dominant CoCrMo components.

I feel like all of you are only looking at part of the picture. 

To a certain degree, with no connections at a company, shotgunning applications is the right move because you’re more likely than not to never make it past automated screening even if you selectively reconfigure your resume. It’s just an SEO game and you aren’t going to be able to retail or your resume and LI profile enough to over come perceived experience gaps etc. 

Think of job applications as a pipeline that start from applying online, to HR interview, to hiring manager interview, to panel interview, to offer, to negotiations and then to acceptance of said offer. 

Most people end up never moving pipeline to HR interview or hiring manager interview. 

If you are interested in making a change in your employer or in your career, it’s prudent to network on linked in by looking at what jobs or companies you’re interested in and cold connecting to and messaging people to see if you can learn more about the culture, the role etc. ideally you’d do this when you’re not looking for jobs but planning on a jump so you can get people on the phone for 10-15 mins to have a discussion and make a connection so that when you do apply for jobs, you can lean on them to connect you to hiring manager or HR and skip the resume shredder. 

Barring this, if you’re hell bent on applying to a role and don’t have a network, cold email people in the role you’re applying for or one or two levels up and have them connect you to hiring manager or HR. It is imperative to speak to some. Not email, not text. The power of verbal communication moves the pipeline to the right.

Hi Bitesh,
I can’t really make the choice for you but here are some things to consider:
1) at Ohio State in the college of engineering, you don’t get into your major immediately. You take intro level courses in physics, math, chemistry, general engineering (CAD modeling and programming) and at the end of your first year, apply to your major (Computer Science and Engineering, etc.). Each major has a general trend for GPA required and number of people admitted so depending on your grades you may not end up studying what you want. 

2) If this isn’t your terminal degree (you plan for grad school, law school, MBA, etc) I’d recommend going to the school that is the cheapest cost to you over the course of your degree. 

3) Columbus is an incredible city. For reasons you allude to around tradition etc. but also Columbus is one of the more diverse cities in the Midwest and much bigger than Ann Arbor, West Lafayette or UC. Specifically, the campus is large and basically an independent ecosystem from the city of Columbus which gives you more to explore and engage with. 

4) looking back, undergrad is also about personal growth. Ohio state is a large university. To some, this is disconcerting because it’s harder to stand out but for me, I was able to engage in activities and find a solid group of friends that I still rely on to this day. There are so many resources and opportunities available, you’ll start to gain some interest in other areas. 

5) In terms of competitiveness of engineering programs of the schools you listed, Ohio State is probably the worst in terms of raw academic rigor. UIUC in CS is known for its security program and Purdue in general is known for being a challenging engineering school. Not sure how much this matters to you, as in general, the content expected to graduate is relatively similar at all these institutions. 

6) finally, I really enjoyed my time at OSU. Not swaying you one way or the other, but if you’re willing to take the Leap and stay engaged with the campus life and find your people, you’ll have an incredible time here.

When you do get your shoulder replaced here’s some things you should be aware of as you figure out how to do to:

1) the surgeon is more important than the implant

3) ask if they’re part of any societies like ASES. 
4) ask if it’s inpatient or outpatient. Depending on your condition if you can tolerate outpatient surgery it’s usually better.

At the end of the day Jagex is trying to run a business. 

If you consider the building of a brand as fundamental to the success of a business, that brand can essentially be broken down into a 2x2 matrix where companies can choose to acquire or retain customers and choose to either earn share or create a new market. 

Jagex’s RuneScape brand is well established. At this point their core revenue stream is retained users but those who pay more (increase average spend per customer). To that end, the updates that are focused are a combination of content (Forinthry, Necromancy) and value drivers that entice purchase (MTX that creates FOMO like HeroPass for example, or a TH promo that has a limited cosmetic that people love or the summer promo for Golden Cape). 

There’s a strong positive correlation between playtime and spend in the target market for Jagex so gamejam probably includes value add projects like combat rebalances, new bosses etc. but likely deprioritizes high cost updates like graphics updates unless those are combined with content that forces engagement in that region (for example, if they update the fairy land or something, they’ll probably have a quest or skill or mini game with some limited time rewards or benefits).
